chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from al-Hudhrami from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): A man married a woman and he has another wife with him. He said: If she is a virgin, he should spend the night with her for seven days; and if she is a mature woman (thayyib), for three nights. This does not contradict the first report because the way to resolve it is to carry the first report on permissibility and the second report on preference, because the preference is that the virgin is not preferred with more than three nights due to the freshness of her wedding, and it is permissible to prefer her with seven nights. As for the non-virgin, she is not preferred with more than three nights, then he returns to equality and emphasizes that.

key_terms.الْخَبَرَ الْأَوَّلَ: the first report (referring to a general rule of equality)
key_terms.الْفَضْلَ: preference/excess (granting one wife more time than the other)
key_terms.بِكْرًا: virgin (a woman who has not been married or consummated marriage before)
key_terms.ثَيِّبًا: mature woman (a woman who has been married and consummated the marriage previously)
key_terms.حِدَثَانَ عُرْسِهَا: freshness of her wedding (the novelty period of marriage)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on the number of nights a husband should spend with a new virgin wife versus a previously married wife?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) resolves the apparent contradiction in marital distribution by distinguishing between the right of preference (fadl) and the right of equality (jawaz). He grants the virgin up to seven nights to accommodate the heightened novelty of her wedding (hidthan 'ursiha), while limiting the mature woman's preference to three nights, after which equal distribution is strictly enforced to ensure justice.
